name: Cardiac Rhabdomyoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and histopathology

criteria.description: Identification of one or more well-circumscribed, hyperechoic cardiac masses on echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Histological confirmation showing large polygonal myocytes with abundant glycogen and spider cells
Presence of tuberous sclerosis complex or related genetic mutation (TSC1 or TSC2)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of characteristic cardiac mass on imaging with or without histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made prenatally or in infancy by echocardiography; genetic testing for TSC is recommended.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intracardiac tumor mass detected by imaging

pathognomonic.notes: Often coexists with neurological and dermatological features of TSC

common.notes: Due to obstruction or altered blood flow
Including ventricular tachycardia or premature beats
Especially in large or multiple tumors

rare.notes: Rare but possible due to arrhythmia
Very rare due to tumor fragmentation

laboratory: Genetic testing positive for TSC1 or TSC2 mutations
Normal routine blood tests unless heart failure present
imaging: Echocardiography showing multiple hyperechoic masses in ventricles
Cardiac MRI confirming tumor size and location
Prenatal ultrasound may detect cardiac masses
genetic: Mutations in TSC1 or TSC2 genes associated with tuberous sclerosis complex
other: Histopathology showing spider cells and glycogen-rich myocytes
Dermatological signs of tuberous sclerosis (e.g., hypomelanotic macules)

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple tissue types on histology
Less commonly associated with tuberous sclerosis

redFlags: Severe heart failure symptoms in infant
references: Goldman M, et al. Cardiac Rhabdomyoma: Clinical Features and Management. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2023.
Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Consensus Conference. Diagnosis and Management Guidelines. 2021.
Maron BJ, et al. Cardiac Tumors in Children. Circulation. 2020.
